# 聯準會不升息，短債反彈、長債卻重挫

## 升息風險暫解，長端卻承受更大壓力

聯準會週三維持利率，債市卻沒有一致慶祝。立即升息的風險解除後，2年期殖利率下降4個基點至4.22%；30年期卻跳升11個基點至5.20%，10年期上升6個基點至4.67%。曲線急遽轉陡，2s10s擴大10個基點至45，2s30s擴大15個基點至98。

9比3的表決，將目標區間維持在3.5%至3.75%。主席Kevin Warsh未清楚交代何時可能緊縮，反而指出市場殖利率上升，已是現有抑制力量的一部分。投資人把預期升息時間往後推，卻要求更高的長期通膨及存續期間補償。美伊再度交火、油價急彈，更強化長債賣壓。10年期名目殖利率升幅全來自通膨補償，更長天期的實質殖利率也上升。

信用借款人同時面對重新定價。7月投資級發行創紀錄，市場流動性承壓，CoreWeave調高貸款利差、加強文件保護，軟體業貸款人則要求更早還款及更好的擔保品保障。融資仍在進行，條件卻愈來愈嚴格。另一方面，澳洲通膨低於預期，帶動短端殖利率下降，顯示美國長債跌勢並非全球一致現象。

## 短率下降，通膨補償卻上升

FOMC連續第七個月維持區間不變。達拉斯總裁Lorie Logan、克里夫蘭總裁Beth Hammack及明尼亞波利斯總裁Neel Kashkari主張升息25個基點，投下反對票。決策排除了會前約35%至40%機率的立即升息，代表性短券殖利率隨2年期下降5至9個基點。但三票異議也說明，下一步未必是寬鬆。

Warsh重申2%通膨目標、否認放寬目標，卻未承諾升息。他認為金融條件已經收緊，使市場本身的調整更重要。30年期殖利率盤中接近5.23%，收5.20%，逼近上次出現在2007年的水準。20年期以上美債指數跌1.64%，1至3年期指數反漲0.06%。

轉折出現在直接反映近期政策的年期之外。即使短端反彈，5年期殖利率仍升2個基點至4.37%。2s10s、2s30s從週二35、83個基點，擴至45、98個基點，幅度遠超過前幾個油價緩和交易日的曲線變化。

抗通膨債呈現不同年期的壓力。10年期實質殖利率維持2.41%，損益兩平通膨率升6個基點至2.26%，完全解釋名目殖利率升幅。30年期實質殖利率升6個基點至2.98%，20年期升4個基點至2.76%；5年期與7年期實質殖利率卻各降6、4個基點，5年期降至2.13%。近期政策壓力緩和，同時伴隨10年期通膨補償提高，以及更長端的實質報酬要求上升。

油價反轉了前三天反彈的基礎。美伊停火空檔結束，美軍遭攻擊後，華府威脅強力回應，布蘭特上漲7.37%至$90.29、WTI漲6.35%至$84.29。兩者雖仍低於上週高點，布蘭特一個月卻高25.42%，WTI高21.75%。央行選擇等待之際，能源再漲，讓通膨壓力自行消退的假設更難成立。

交換市場調整的是升息時間，而非放棄升息。會後9月升息機率約60%，到12月才完全計入一次；前一日則已完全計入9月升息。三票異議保留緊縮方向，有限指引卻使時點更不確定。

成交也集中在殖利率變動最大的區段。FINRA公布名目付息公債交易面額$1.15兆，較7月28日增加10.3%。20年以上成交增36.9%，7至10年增30.4%，3至5年卻減14.2%。這是成交量，不是淨流入流出，但顯示長端調整發生在活躍交易中。

供給仍是另一項疑慮。摩根大通估計，未來四個財政年度融資缺口達$3.7兆，美國財政部終須修改未來數季付息券標售規模不變的承諾。策略師預期，下一次季度再融資仍會保留原措辭，避免期中選舉前宣布增加存續期間供給，本身就推動曲線轉陡。不改指引能延後公告衝擊，不能消除借款需求。

2、5、10、30年期殖利率一個月已各升15、25、29、33個基點。週三短端卸下立即升息的溢價，長天期投資人卻面對更昂貴的通膨及供給風險。

## 發行創紀錄，貸款人談判籌碼增加

紐約聯準銀行週三公布、觀察截至7月24日的企業債壓力指標，顯示信用市場內部分歧。整體指數從6月底0.16降至0.15，投資級子指數卻從0.25升至0.30，為2023年11月以來最高、約歷史第68百分位。7月投資級發行約$1,320億創紀錄，部分來自AI借款，使新券定價與次級流動性更困難，但尚非全面市場失靈。

投資級利差為80個基點，7月初為74個基點。週三基金損失也反映利率衝擊，LQD跌0.57%，HYG、JNK各跌約0.23%。20年期以上AAA至A企業債指數跌1.34%，BBB指數跌1.30%，同時長美債跌1.64%。

CoreWeave的$26億延遲動用定期貸款，顯示AI借款條件正在改變。利差最多擴大125個基點至基準加550個基點，發行價從99降至97，並在週四訂單截止前加強債權人保障。融資用於GPU及其他設備，提供Anthropic、Jane Street與Hudson River Trading「照付不議」合約下的算力，利息只按已動用資金計算。

CoreWeave今年預期投入逾$340億基建，5年期違約保障成本7月已升逾50%，達12月以來最高。相較之下，先前$31億GPU擔保融資曾吸引$190億訂單。投資人已不再只因設備擔保及合約需求，就接受原來條件。

QTS可能很快提供另一項比較。潛在$54億Microsoft承租資料中心融資，包括約$49億擔保債及$5億定期貸款。其近期貸款已從99.5跌至97.75，4月債券利差則從約美債加138擴至239個基點。既有券更便宜之際再發新債，需要多少讓利，將成為交易關鍵。

軟體借款人也遇到更明確的債權人待遇限制。Proofpoint修改$50億條款修訂暨展期交易，因貸款人要求防止移轉擔保品及選擇性買回。公司同意加入「omni blocker」資產移轉限制、未來買回要約平等對待債權人，並修改約二十多項條文。方案把2028年到期延至2030年，利差425至450個基點，發行價98至98.5。

壓力不限單一公司。2028年美國槓桿貸款到期約$3,000億，近三分之一與科技相關，包括許多在2021年融資、由私募股權支持的軟體公司。Imprivata最近延長$12億貸款，利差從300升至375個基點。貸款人同時評估AI對未來獲利的影響，以及同意再次展延前需要哪些保障。

歐洲部分投資人希望過程中就拿回現金。Paysafe提出每年攤還原始本金5%，將$8.14億及€5.86億貸款延長兩年至2030年。條件包括500個基點利差、95價格買進而最終按100償還。投資人也表示，若think-cell延長目前Euribor加425個基點的€7.2億貸款，將要求攤還本金。

2008年以來，歐洲這類具份量的攤還安排相當少見。提早收回本金，可減少對單次未來再融資的依賴；但CLO需求仍限制貸款人議價空間。約30%投資人拒絕凱雷支持的AutoForm展期，整體需求卻仍讓其€6.72億貸款收窄利差、延至2032年。

SoftBank取得日圓資金，但代價不低。公司發行JPY900億，把3年期擴大至JPY800億、5年期保留JPY100億。票息各3.270%、3.886%，較日本公債高165、190個基點，為今年同年期日本企業最高。投資人偏好短年期，5年期訂單僅約1.2倍。

發行支應逾$600億OpenAI承諾，另有已增加21家貸款人的$400億過橋貸款。至少$60億保證金融資談判則停滯，原先目標為$100億、後來下修。日圓、美元、歐元、零售次順位及銀行融資，擴大SoftBank選擇，卻未消除槓桿及AI集中曝險的成本。

銀行也在騰出資產負債表空間。ING準備以約$100億貸款進行重大風險移轉交易，包括約$60億美歐專案融資、涵蓋資料中心，以及€35億荷蘭中小企業貸款。移轉風險部分各占參考組合約7%、6%，逾10%票息吸引願意承擔第一損失的投資人。2026年全球SRT發行預估創紀錄$450億，2025年為$410億。

保險資金管道也受到檢視。Delaware Life重編申報後，評等機構估計關係人資產占比為40%至42%，而不是原本約3%至5%。若這類持有受到更嚴格監督，私人貸款轉入保險公司資產負債表的速度可能下降。較高貸款利差、更強文件保障之外，大型融資計畫又多了一項潛在資金限制。

## 澳洲因通膨數據上漲，日本薪資升勢則擴大

澳洲核心通膨較低，債券逆美國跌勢而漲。第2季截尾平均CPI年增3.6%，低於預估3.7%；季增0.8%，低於0.9%。市場把今年再升息機率從逾90%降至約50%，澳元最多跌0.5%，3年期殖利率跌11個基點。在2026年稍早已升息三次後，央行8月11日有更多空間等待。

細節未全然令人放心。可貿易財通膨1.5%，受惠於進口能源價格及暫時燃料稅減免；不可貿易財卻達4.9%。核心仍高於2%至3%目標，油價再漲也威脅外部成本緩解。數據降低了再升息的急迫性，未解決整體前景。

歐元區薪資預測，也遠低於先前通膨循環高點。ECB追蹤指標預估協商薪資第3、4季增2.6%，2027年第1季增2.7%，對照2024年高點5.2%。官員表示，部分增加是舊的一次性給付退出比較基期造成。數據讓央行有時間評估能源傳導，9月升息仍有可能。

英國借款需求比高利率可能暗示的更有韌性。6月房貸核准從兩年多低點回升至58,200件，高於57,100件預估，無擔保借款增加£18億。但7月29日平均5年房貸利率達5.66%，伊朗戰前為4.83%。英國央行仍須權衡低成長與能源通膨，而非面對需求崩跌。

日本最低工資建議升幅，擴大了進一步政策正常化的理由。厚生勞動省小組建議提高4.9%、即JPY55，至每小時JPY1,176，為史上第二大增幅。雖小於去年6.3%，卻可把薪資成長擴及大型企業之外；主要工會已連續第三年爭取逾5%調薪。日本銀行6月升息至1%後，這項建議增加了後續評估的薪資證據。

GPIF也在適應更不穩定的國內債市。基金五年來首次任命三家主動式日本債券經理人，截至3月年度，日本債券虧5.1%，整體卻賺16.5%。25%國內債券配置目標提供相當規模，主動委任則增加年期與信用曝險調整空間。較高本地殖利率可吸引資金回流，但不代表日本公債曲線每一點都有穩定買盤。

加拿大央行討論顯示，維持立場之內也有分歧。央行連續第六次維持2.25%，預估成長從2026年0.7%，加快至2027、2028年各1.8%。部分官員懷疑復甦持久性，另一些擔心中期通膨預期上升；供給過剩、單位勞動成本放慢及租金通膨下降，則支持耐心。紀錄維持當前政策，卻顯示下一步的不確定性。

## 美元轉弱有利新興貨幣，長美元債卻下跌

聯準會維持利率後，新興市場貨幣上漲，長天期外幣債卻走弱。貨幣指數漲0.3%，美元指數跌0.59%至100.78；EMB跌0.66%，15年期以上新興市場美元主權債指數跌0.60%。較高長美債殖利率，壓過匯率帶來的緩解。

即使IMF就新$19億方案達成協議，玻利維亞債券仍小跌。官方支持前景未消除執行及債務可持續性疑慮，走勢與區域貨幣較強的背景不同。

巴西7月初通膨從6月中4.8%降至4.52%，支持8月5日連續第四次降息25個基點至14%的預期。但勞動市場強勁、政府財政與信貸刺激，仍可能使需求相對3%通膨目標偏強。本地降息理由取決於持續降溫，不只是聯準會選擇不動。

印度儲蓄則支持銀行資本發行。印度國家銀行近兩年後重返市場，募集INR469.1億永久AT1，票息7.75%、5年可贖回、本地AA+評等，訂單超過INR300億基本規模兩倍。資金支持成長近17%、超過INR49兆的貸款組合。

菲律賓擬議勞工所得稅減免，使財政整頓更困難。每年收入可能減少最多PHP600億、約$9.78億，而2026年已計畫借款PHP2.68兆。第1季債務為GDP的65.2%，高於開發中經濟體常用的60%參考線，廉價疫情債務以現有殖利率再融資，也提高了利息負擔。要把2025年5.6%赤字降至2030年3.5%，減稅之餘須有替代收入或支出節制。

印度則準備立法，正式落實外資投資主權債的減稅，尋求更廣外部買方。方案可改善參與，但立法及後續流量仍未實現。美元下降緩解一項共同外部限制，本地政策與融資結構仍然重要。

## 油金齊漲，股票回落

能源衝擊再起，伴隨較全面股市下跌。S&P 500跌1.52%、Nasdaq 100跌2.06%、半導體跌5.33%，後者連續第五天下跌，一週及一個月跌幅達15.82%、20.87%。VIX升13.45%至20.66，AI資本回報疑慮與聯準會後更廣泛賣壓交疊。

黃金漲2.78%至$4,148.60，美元跌0.59%。連同油價及長美債殖利率上升，較像通膨與政策疑慮，而非全面搶美元現金。2年期殖利率下降，沒有讓長存續期間資產或股票的環境變得更寬鬆。

高收益債基金跌幅遠小於LQD，新興市場貨幣也上漲。壓力很大，卻仍不平均：能源及政策不確定性壓抑長主權債，科技借款人則面對回報、融資條件與債權保護的質疑。

## 薪資、季度再融資與AI訂單，檢驗新的價格

7月31日僱用成本指數，以及後續通膨和勞動數據，將有助判斷9月緊縮是否仍是最可能下一步。若薪資偏強、布蘭特在$90附近或更高，會後2年期反彈可能受挑戰；勞動成本較弱、局勢再降溫則有利。更長端的損益兩平通膨率，以及20至30年實質殖利率，將顯示通膨疑慮是否穩定。

下一次季度再融資另有供給問題。維持付息券規模指引，可減輕立即公告衝擊；若措辭讓擴大標售更接近，曲線就須面對估計四年$3.7兆缺口。這與聯準會選擇哪一次會議行動，是不同考量。

CoreWeave週四截止，將顯示基準加最多550個基點、97價格及更強保障下的需求。潛在$54億QTS融資，則可對照已變便宜的流通券。訂單及次級表現會顯示，貸款人認為讓利已足夠，還是要求更多折價與控制。

英國央行7月30日、日本銀行7月31日決策。英國平均5年房貸5.66%，尚未阻止借款；日本建議最低工資升4.9%，在6月政策利率升至1%後，增加正常化理由。兩家央行指引與日圓反應，將在美債長端已無法依賴前幾日油價緩和行情時，影響海外債券需求。

overall_summary.session_narrative:
聯準會維持3.5%至3.75%，三名官員主張升息25個基點。2年期殖利率降4個基點至4.22%，10年期卻升6個基點至4.67%，30年期升11個基點至5.20%。10年期升幅全來自通膨補償，更長端實質殖利率也上升。美伊再度交火，布蘭特漲7.37%至$90.29。

市場延後升息、沒有放棄升息，曲線大幅轉陡。9月升息機率降至約60%，12月才完全計入一次。長端成交活躍，摩根大通估計四年融資缺口$3.7兆，也增添存續期間壓力。

信用供給的壓力更具體。紐約聯準銀行截至7月24日的投資級壓力指標上升，整體指標卻下降。CoreWeave貸款利差擴至最多550個基點、價格降至97，軟體借款人提供更強擔保品保護及更早本金攤還。澳洲因通膨較低而反彈，新興貨幣上漲，長美元債卻下跌。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# Fed hold lifts short Treasuries, but long bonds sell off sharply

## The Fed removes one risk and leaves the long end exposed

The Fed held rates on Wednesday, but the bond market delivered anything but a uniform relief rally. Two-year Treasury yields fell 4 basis points to 4.22% as the threat of an immediate increase passed. Thirty-year yields jumped 11 basis points to 5.20%, while the 10-year rose 6 to 4.67%. The curve steepened abruptly: 2s10s widened 10 basis points to 45 and 2s30s widened 15 to 98.

The 9–3 vote kept the target range at 3.5%–3.75%. Chairman Kevin Warsh offered little guidance on when the Fed might tighten, instead pointing to higher market yields as part of the restraint already in place. Investors pushed the expected hike later, but demanded more compensation for long-term inflation and duration. Renewed US-Iran hostilities and a sharp rebound in oil reinforced the selloff. The entire increase in the nominal 10-year yield came through breakevens, while real yields rose farther out the curve.

Credit borrowers faced their own repricing. Record July high-grade supply was straining liquidity, CoreWeave widened loan terms and strengthened documents, and software lenders sought earlier repayments and better collateral protection. Financing continued, but the concessions were becoming more demanding. Meanwhile, a softer Australian inflation report drove its short yields lower, underscoring that the US long-bond selloff was not a uniform global move.

## Short rates fall as inflation compensation rises

The FOMC left its range unchanged for a seventh consecutive month. Dallas President Lorie Logan, Cleveland President Beth Hammack and Minneapolis President Neel Kashkari dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. The hold removed a risk priced at roughly 35%–40% before the meeting. Representative bill yields fell 5–9 basis points alongside the two-year decline, but the dissents left no suggestion that the next move would necessarily be easier policy.

Warsh reiterated the 2% inflation objective and rejected a softer target without committing to an increase. His argument that financial conditions had already tightened put more weight on what markets themselves were doing. The 30-year yield briefly approached 5.23% before closing at 5.20%, near levels last seen in 2007. A 20-year-plus Treasury index lost 1.64%, against a 0.06% gain in the one-to-three-year index.

The turn occurred beyond the immediate policy horizon. Five-year yields rose 2 basis points to 4.37% despite the short-end rally. From Tuesday's 35 and 83 basis points, 2s10s and 2s30s widened to 45 and 98. The move overwhelmed the modest curve changes of the preceding oil-relief sessions.

Inflation-linked bonds showed different pressures by maturity. At ten years, the real yield stayed at 2.41% and the breakeven rose 6 basis points to 2.26%, accounting for the full nominal increase. At 30 years, the real yield climbed 6 basis points to 2.98%; the 20-year rose 4 to 2.76%. Five- and seven-year real yields instead declined 6 and 4 basis points, with the five-year at 2.13%. Near-term policy relief was therefore accompanied by higher inflation compensation at ten years and a larger real-yield burden farther out.

Oil reversed the premise of the previous three-day rally. Brent rose 7.37% to $90.29 and WTI 6.35% to $84.29 after the pause in US-Iran fighting ended and Washington threatened a forceful response to an attack on US forces. Both remained below the prior week's peaks, but Brent was 25.42% higher over a month and WTI 21.75% higher. The renewed increase made it harder to assume that energy pressure would fade while policymakers waited.

Swaps shifted the expected timing of tightening rather than abandoning it. September hike odds were around 60% after the decision, with a full increase not priced until December. The previous close had fully priced September. Three dissents preserved the tightening bias, while limited guidance made the date less certain.

Trading was heavy where yields moved most. FINRA reported $1.15 trillion of nominal-coupon par traded, 10.3% above July 28. Activity beyond 20 years increased 36.9% and the seven-to-ten-year bucket 30.4%, while three-to-five-year par fell 14.2%. These are turnover figures, not net flows, but they show that the long-end adjustment took place in an active market.

Supply remained a separate concern. JPMorgan estimated a $3.7 trillion financing gap over the next four fiscal years and expected Treasury eventually to revise its assurance of stable coupon auction sizes for several quarters. Its strategists thought officials would leave the wording unchanged at the next refunding, wary that an announcement of more duration before the midterms could itself steepen the curve. Keeping the guidance could postpone that announcement effect, not eliminate the financing need.

Monthly yield increases now stood at 15, 25, 29 and 33 basis points at two, five, ten and 30 years. Wednesday relieved the immediate Fed-event premium at the front while leaving longer-maturity investors facing more expensive inflation and supply risks.

## Record supply gives lenders more leverage

The New York Fed's corporate distress measures, released Wednesday with observations through July 24, showed a widening gap within credit. The overall index eased to 0.15 from 0.16 in late June, but the investment-grade sub-index rose to 0.30 from 0.25, its highest since November 2023 and around the 68th historical percentile. About $132 billion of July high-grade issuance, a record helped by AI borrowing, was making new-issue pricing and secondary liquidity more difficult without producing broad market dysfunction.

Investment-grade spreads stood at 80 basis points, versus 74 at the start of July. Wednesday's fund losses also reflected the rates shock: LQD fell 0.57%, while HYG and JNK each lost about 0.23%. The 20-year-plus AAA-to-A corporate index declined 1.34% and its BBB counterpart 1.30%, alongside the 1.64% long-Treasury loss.

CoreWeave's $2.6 billion delayed-draw term loan showed the changing terms available to AI borrowers. Pricing widened as much as 125 basis points to as high as 550 over the benchmark, the offer price fell from 99 to 97, and creditor protections were strengthened ahead of Thursday's order deadline. The financing supports GPUs and other equipment for take-or-pay capacity used by Anthropic, Jane Street and Hudson River Trading, with interest charged only on drawn funds.

CoreWeave is expected to spend more than $34 billion on infrastructure this year. Its five-year default-protection cost had risen more than 50% in July to the highest since December. That contrasted with an earlier $3.1 billion GPU-backed financing that attracted $19 billion of orders. Investors were no longer treating equipment collateral and contracted demand as sufficient reasons to accept the original terms.

QTS could soon provide another comparison. A potential $5.4 billion Microsoft-leased data-center financing would comprise about $4.9 billion of secured bonds and a $500 million term loan. Its recent loan had slipped from 99.5 to 97.75, while its April bond spread widened from roughly 138 to 239 basis points over Treasuries. The proposed transaction would arrive with existing paper already cheaper, raising the question of how much concession the next deal needs.

Software borrowers were encountering more explicit restrictions on creditor treatment. Proofpoint reworked a $5 billion amend-and-extend after lenders demanded protection against collateral transfers and selective repurchases. It agreed to an “omni blocker,” equal treatment in future buyback offers and changes to roughly two dozen provisions. The proposal extends a 2028 maturity to 2030 at 425–450 basis points over the benchmark and an issue price of 98–98.5.

The urgency was not confined to one borrower. Roughly $300 billion of US leveraged loans mature in 2028, almost a third tied to technology companies, including many buyout-backed software businesses financed in 2021. Imprivata recently extended a $1.2 billion loan at 375 basis points over the benchmark, up from 300. Lenders were considering both AI's effect on future earnings and the protections needed before agreeing to another maturity extension.

In Europe, some wanted cash back along the way. Paysafe offered annual amortization of 5% of original principal to extend $814 million and €586 million of loans by two years to 2030. Terms included a 500-basis-point margin and a price of 95 for debt repayable at 100. Investors also indicated they would seek amortization on a possible extension of think-cell's €720 million loan, currently at Euribor plus 425 basis points.

Meaningful amortization had been rare in Europe since 2008. Bringing repayment forward reduces reliance on a single future refinancing, but CLO demand still limited how far lenders could press. About 30% of investors rejected Carlyle-backed AutoForm's extension, yet broader demand allowed its €672 million loan to tighten and extend to 2032.

SoftBank found yen funding at a high price. It sold JPY90 billion, increasing the three-year tranche to JPY80 billion and retaining JPY10 billion at five years. Coupons of 3.270% and 3.886%, respectively 165 and 190 basis points over JGBs, were the highest paid this year by a domestic corporate borrower at those maturities. The five-year book covered only about 1.2 times the bonds, as investors favored the shorter term.

The sale supports more than $60 billion of OpenAI commitments alongside a $40 billion bridge loan that has added 21 lenders. Talks for at least $6 billion of margin financing had stalled after an earlier $10 billion target was reduced. Access to yen, dollar, euro, retail subordinated and bank funding broadened SoftBank's choices, but did not remove the cost of its leverage and AI concentration.

Banks were also seeking room on their balance sheets. ING prepared significant-risk-transfer deals on about $10 billion of loans: roughly $6 billion of US and European project finance, including data centers, and €3.5 billion of Dutch SME exposure. The risk pieces represented about 7% and 6% of those portfolios. Coupons above 10% attracted investors willing to absorb first losses; global SRT issuance was projected at a record $45 billion in 2026, versus $41 billion in 2025.

The insurance channel faced scrutiny of its own. Following a reporting restatement, rating agencies estimated Delaware Life's affiliated assets at 40%–42% of total assets rather than roughly 3%–5%. Tighter oversight of such holdings could slow the placement of private loans on insurer balance sheets. Alongside higher loan margins and stronger documents, that put another potential constraint on the capital available for large funding programs.

## Australia rallies on inflation data as Japan's wage case strengthens

Australian bonds moved against the US selloff after a softer core inflation report. Second-quarter trimmed-mean CPI rose 3.6% from a year earlier versus 3.7% expected, and 0.8% quarter on quarter versus 0.9%. Markets cut the chance of another RBA increase this year to about 50% from more than 90%. The Australian dollar fell as much as 0.5% and the three-year yield dropped 11 basis points, giving the bank more room to wait on August 11 after three increases earlier in 2026.

The details were less uniformly reassuring. Tradables inflation was 1.5%, helped by imported-energy prices and temporary fuel-tax relief, while non-tradables ran at 4.9%. Core inflation remained above the 2%–3% target, and oil's renewed rise threatened the external relief. The release reduced the urgency of another increase without settling the outlook.

Euro-area wage projections also remained well below the earlier inflation cycle's peak. The ECB tracker put negotiated pay growth at 2.6% in the third and fourth quarters and 2.7% in the first quarter of 2027, compared with 5.2% in 2024. Officials described part of the increase as mechanical as old one-off payments left the comparison. The figures gave policymakers time to assess energy pass-through, even while September tightening remained possible.

British borrowing was more resilient than its high interest costs might suggest. June mortgage approvals recovered to 58,200 from a more than two-year low, above the 57,100 forecast, and unsecured borrowing increased £1.8 billion. The average five-year mortgage rate nevertheless reached 5.66% on July 29, up from 4.83% before the Iran war. The BOE still had to balance slow growth with energy inflation rather than a collapse in demand.

Japan's proposed minimum-wage increase broadened the case for further normalization. A labor ministry panel recommended a 4.9%, or JPY55, rise to JPY1,176 an hour, the second-largest on record. It was smaller than last year's 6.3%, but would extend pay gains beyond large employers after major unions secured more than 5% for a third year. The recommendation added to the wage evidence the BOJ was assessing after its June increase to a 1% policy rate.

GPIF was adapting to a less stable domestic bond market. It appointed three active Japanese bond managers for the first time in five years after losing 5.1% on domestic bonds in the year to March, despite a 16.5% overall return. A 25% domestic-bond allocation target gave the fund substantial capacity, while active mandates allowed more discretion over maturity and credit exposure. Higher local yields could draw savings home without ensuring a steady bid at every point on the JGB curve.

Bank of Canada deliberations showed a split within an unchanged stance. The bank had held 2.25% for a sixth meeting and forecast growth accelerating from 0.7% in 2026 to 1.8% in both 2027 and 2028. Some officials doubted the recovery's durability; others worried about rising medium-term inflation expectations. Excess supply, slower unit labor costs and easing rent inflation argued for patience. The minutes left the current stance intact while exposing the uncertainty around the next move.

## A softer dollar helps EM currencies, not long dollar bonds

Emerging-market currencies rose after the Fed hold, but long hard-currency bonds lost ground. A currency gauge gained 0.3% as the dollar index fell 0.59% to 100.78. EMB declined 0.66% and a 15-year-plus EM dollar sovereign index 0.60%, with higher long Treasury yields outweighing the currency relief.

Bolivian bonds edged lower despite agreement on a new $1.9 billion IMF program. The reaction showed that investors still had concerns about implementation and debt sustainability even with prospective official support. It stood apart from the firmer regional currency backdrop.

Brazil's early-July inflation eased to 4.52% from 4.8% in mid-June, supporting expectations of a fourth consecutive quarter-point cut to 14% on August 5. A strong labor market and government fiscal and credit stimulus could still sustain demand relative to the 3% inflation target. The local easing case depended on continued disinflation, not simply on the Fed's decision to hold.

Indian savings supported bank-capital issuance. State Bank of India raised INR46.91 billion of perpetual AT1 after nearly two years away, with a 7.75% coupon, five-year call and local AA+ rating. Bids exceeded twice the INR30 billion base size. The capital supports a loan book that grew almost 17% to more than INR49 trillion.

In the Philippines, proposed worker income-tax cuts would make fiscal consolidation harder. Annual revenue could fall by as much as PHP60 billion, or about $978 million, against planned 2026 borrowing of PHP2.68 trillion. Debt stood at 65.2% of GDP in the first quarter, above the commonly cited 60% developing-economy benchmark, and refinancing cheap pandemic debt was raising the interest burden. Moving the deficit from 5.6% of GDP in 2025 to 3.5% by 2030 would require replacement revenue or spending restraint alongside the relief.

India was preparing legislation to formalize tax cuts for foreign investors in sovereign bonds, seeking a broader external buyer base. The plan could improve participation, but enactment and subsequent flows were still to come. Across these cases, domestic policy and funding structures mattered even as the weaker dollar eased one shared external constraint.

## Oil and gold rise as equities retreat

The renewed energy shock accompanied a broad equity decline. The S&P 500 fell 1.52%, the Nasdaq 100 2.06% and semiconductors 5.33%, their fifth consecutive loss. Chip-sector declines reached 15.82% over a week and 20.87% over a month. VIX climbed 13.45% to 20.66 as concern over AI capital returns met the wider post-Fed selloff.

Gold rose 2.78% to $4,148.60 while the dollar fell 0.59%. Together with higher oil and long Treasury yields, those moves pointed toward inflation and policy concerns rather than a general scramble for dollars. The fall in two-year yields had not translated into easier conditions for long-duration assets or equities.

High-yield funds lost much less than LQD and emerging-market currencies strengthened. The pressure was substantial, but still uneven: energy and policy uncertainty weighed on long sovereign debt, while technology borrowers faced doubts about returns, financing terms and creditor protection.

## Wages, refunding and AI orders test the new prices

The July 31 Employment Cost Index and subsequent inflation and labor releases will help determine whether September tightening remains the likely next step. Firm wages with Brent near or above $90 could challenge the post-meeting two-year rally; softer labor costs and renewed de-escalation would support it. At longer maturities, breakevens and 20- to 30-year real yields will show whether inflation concern is settling down.

The next quarterly refunding adds the supply question. Stable coupon-size guidance could limit an immediate announcement shock, while language bringing larger auctions closer would confront the curve with the estimated $3.7 trillion four-year gap. It is a separate consideration from the Fed's choice of meeting date.

CoreWeave's Thursday deadline will reveal demand at up to 550 basis points, a 97 price and stronger protections. The potential $5.4 billion QTS financing then offers another test against cheaper outstanding debt. Orderbooks and secondary performance will show whether lenders consider those concessions adequate or seek further discounts and control.

The BOE decides on July 30 and BOJ on July 31. Britain's 5.66% average five-year mortgage rate has not yet stopped borrowing; Japan's proposed 4.9% minimum-wage increase adds to the case for normalization after June's move to 1%. Their guidance and the yen's response will shape foreign bond demand at a time when the Treasury long end can no longer count on the preceding oil-relief rally.
